test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 17 Sept, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the tenure of office for the Chief Election Commissioner?

options.text: 6 years or up to the age of 65 years
5 years or up to the age of 65 years
5 years or up to the age of 60 years
6 years or up to the age of 60 years

solution:
The correct answer is __**6 years or up to the age of 65 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) is **6 years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.**
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office **only through impeachment by Parliament** for proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• The CEC and other Election Commissioners have the same powers, salary, allowances, and other perquisites as are available to a judge of the **Supreme Court of India.**
 
• The concept of an independent Election Commission was introduced to ensure free and fair elections in India, as per the provisions of **Article 324** of the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI)**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at both the national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The Election Commission operates under the authority of Constitution per Article 324, and subsequently enacted Representation of the People Act.
 
• The commission has the powers to monitor the election process, including the preparation of electoral rolls, ensuring the model code of conduct, and scrutinizing election expenses of candidates.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)**
 
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner heads the Election Commission of India and oversees the entire electoral process.
 
• Appointed by the President of India, the CEC ensures that the election process is conducted in a free, fair, and impartial manner.
 
• The CEC can only be removed through a process similar to that of a judge of the Supreme Court, which requires a two-thirds majority in Parliament.
 
• The CEC’s role is critical in maintaining the sanctity of the democratic process in India.
